title: BACE: Applied Mathematics - BACE - Applied Mathematics - Percent Solutions
subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: How many grams of agarose are needed to prepare **50 mL** of a **2.5% (w/v)** agarose gel?
questions.explain: Percent (w/v) means grams per 100 mL. A 2.5% solution means 2.5 g in 100 mL. For 50 mL (which is half of 100 mL), you need half the mass: $$2.5 \text{ g} \times \frac{50 \text{ mL}}{100 \text{ mL}} = 1.25 \text{ g}$$.
questions.subject: BACE - Applied Mathematics

questions.q: You need to make **70% (v/v) ethanol** from a 95% stock solution. How much 95% ethanol is needed to make **200 mL** of the 70% solution?
questions.explain: Use $$C_1V_1 = C_2V_2$$ where concentrations are %. $$(95\%)(V_1) = (70\%)(200 \text{ mL})$$ ​$$V_1 = \frac{70 \times 200}{95} = \frac{14000}{95} \approx 147.368 \text{ mL}$$ Rounding to one decimal place gives **147.4 mL**.

questions.q: Calculate the volume of solute needed to prepare **500 mL** of a **5% (v/v)** bleach solution.
questions.explain: 5% (v/v) means 5 mL of solute per 100 mL of solution. $$5 \text{ mL solute} \times \frac{500 \text{ mL solution}}{100 \text{ mL solution}} = 25 \text{ mL solute}$$
